answer.answer: The retained passages support cryptocurrency’s capacity to be trust property, but ownership depended on the particular terms, consent and party relationship. They do not establish that every customer—or token holder—has a beneficial interest. The 2025 decision distinguishes non-consenting customers’ pooled beneficial interests, ETD holders’ breach-of-trust claims and Samara’s unsecured claim against Gatecoin. Transferring any proposition to a Product Provider requires a justified legal analogy and actual contractual, ownership and regulatory facts; neither Gatecoin decision supplies a test for fulfilling paragraph 10 of 26EC22. Later treatment and the scenario-seven inconsistency remain unresolved.

claims.proposition: The 2023 judgment treats cryptocurrency as property capable of trust, while rejecting a trust under the 2018 terms for customers subject to those terms and preserving the non-consenting-customer exception.
claims.status: Supported by retained conclusion; general application not established

support.quote: Cryptocurrency is “property” and is capable of being held on trust
However, the terms of the 2018 T&C show that there was no certainty of intention to create a trust over the cryptocurrencies held by Gatecoin
Except the Non-Consenting Customers, the 2018 T&C applied to, and governed the relationship between all the Customers (be it Group A, B or C customers) and Gatecoin

claims.inference: The passage expressly distinguishes capacity to hold cryptocurrency on trust from whether a trust actually arose under the relevant relationship.
missing_premises: For another customer or product: applicable terms, consent, trust intention, subject matter and beneficiaries.
Full reasons and subsequent treatment sufficient to establish the scope and authority of the proposition.

claims.proposition: Ownership terminology and an agency or brokerage relationship are relevant but not conclusive evidence of a trust.
claims.status: Supported as quoted reasoning; target application conditional

support.quote: The words used by the parties such as ‘trust’, ‘custody’, ‘belonging’, ‘ownership’, ‘title’, may be persuasive, but they are not conclusive in favour of the recognition of B’s proprietary interest in the property, if the terms of the agreement or relationship, viewed objectively, compel a different conclusion.

The identification of a relationship in which A is B’s agent or broker is not conclusive of a conclusion that A is, in relation to the property, B’s trustee, although it may be a pointer towards that conclusion.

claims.inference: These are principles quoted from Re Lehman Brothers in the retained Gatecoin reasoning. They support examining the objectively assessed relationship rather than inferring a trust from labels or an intermediary role alone.
missing_premises: The complete agreement and conduct between the particular parties concerning the identified property.
The surrounding reasoning establishing how the quoted principles were applied.

claims.proposition: The 2025 classification is evidence-sensitive: scenarios one to four presumptively preserve non-consenting status; scenarios five and six presumptively exclude it but permit contrary proof.
claims.status: Supported by retained paragraph 8; individual classification unresolved

support.quote: The customers should be regarded as NCCs unless there is evidence to show that they have accessed or used the Platform to effect the transactions

The transactions described in the 5th to 6th scenarios on their face required the customers to access or use the Platform to effect them and, prima facie, the customers fall outside the definition of NCC.
However, if the customers are able to prove that they gave the instruction to Gatecoin before the Relevant Date or without using the Platform, they should be regarded as NCCs.

claims.inference: A ledger entry after the relevant date does not by itself establish customer access or consent. Paragraph 8 distinguishes automated events from transactions apparently requiring access, subject to contrary evidence.
missing_premises: The customer's transaction category, instructions, timing and actual platform access.
The full definition of non-consenting customers and applicable evidential requirements.

claims.proposition: The 2025 passages distinguish pooled beneficial ownership, Gatecoin's assets, breach-of-trust claims and unsecured creditor claims.

support.quote: Each NCC is a beneficial tenant-in-common in a pool of cryptocurrency and fiat currency.
The Currencies recorded in BlueFire’s accounts are assets of Gatecoin.
ETD represents a cause of action by ETD Holder against Gatecoin for breach of trust.
Gatecoin does not hold the Subject Bitcoins or the Specified Account on trust for Mr Samara.
Mr Samara is only an unsecured creditor to the extent of his claim less the amount he already received through execution of the HCA Judgment.

claims.inference: The disposition assigns different rights to different relationships. A beneficial interest or claim arising in one relationship cannot simply be attributed to another party against Gatecoin.
missing_premises: The precise claimant, defendant, property, account and contractual or trust relationship in the proposed application.
Full reasons for the BlueFire, ETD and Samara conclusions before extending them beyond the stated results.

claims.proposition: Scenario seven remains an unresolved textual tension, preventing a complete automatic customer classifier.

support.quote: The transactions described in the 7th scenario did not exist and the customers should not be regarded as NCC.

The 5th to 7th scenarios prima facie fall outside the definition of NCC but if the customers can prove that they gave the relevant instructions to Gatecoin before the Relevant Date or without using the Platform, they should be regarded as NCCs.

Any Customer who claims to have transactions enumerated in paragraphs 1.2(b) shall notify the Liquidators and provide evidence to the Liquidators in support of such a claim within 21 days from the date hereof.

claims.inference: Paragraph 8 rejects scenario seven as factually absent, whereas paragraph 95 includes it in a rebuttable exclusion. The annexure adds specific categories and proof requirements. The supplied excerpts do not justify automatically harmonising these formulations.
missing_premises: Checked full reasons, operative order and annexure structure, including their intended relationship.
Any correction or later judicial clarification of scenario seven.

claims.proposition: Transfer to a Product Provider under 26EC22 requires separate legal and factual premises; trust status neither establishes nor exhausts regulatory compliance.
claims.status: Source-grounded deduction; transfer and fulfillment not established

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.
the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

claims.inference: Gatecoin may inform analysis of what ownership rights records should reflect. It does not, on these excerpts, interpret 26EC22 or establish that retaining responsibility, supervising a contractor or recording an interest fulfills its requirements. This transfer is a proposed analogy, not a holding.
missing_premises: Applicable edition of 26EC22, assessment interval, product authorisation conditions and any amendments or relaxations.
The entity's Product Provider role and any distinct trustee, register-keeper, custodian or intermediary capacity.
Governing law, constitutive documents, customer terms and consent, title to tokens versus underlying interests, settlement finality and the outsourcing chain.
A justified identification of the relevant Gatecoin proposition, its authority and materially comparable facts.
An applicable standard for retained responsibility and fulfillment, plus actual evidence of authority, supervisory conduct, operational soundness and proper ownership records.

rival_readings: Scenario seven: paragraph 8 supports factual absence and exclusion from NCC status; paragraph 95's wording supports prima facie exclusion with an opportunity for contrary proof. Neither is silently preferred.

Transfer: Gatecoin's objective assessment of ownership relationships may assist analysis of a tokenised product. Its exchange-insolvency findings may also be materially distinguishable from that product's governing terms and regulatory responsibilities.
unresolved: The 2025 passage records and uses the 2023 conclusions; it does not establish complete subsequent treatment of either judgment. Binding force and the precise ratio for the target dispute remain unverified.
Only selected passages are supplied. Candidate assertions of full-reasons review are not independent verification of those reasons or rendered DOCX fidelity.
The candidate case manifests reuse one source hash, while the corpus lists different hashes for the two source files; the provenance discrepancy is unexplained.
The scenario-seven tension and annexure relationship remain open.
No target Product Provider facts or applicable fulfillment standard are supplied. Formal parsing, graph acceptance and rule roundtrips cannot supply these premises or establish legal truth.
